title: Rational fixed point for a split torus on a proper scheme
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $T$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with unit multiplication, and let $X$ be a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $a:T\times_kX\to X$ is a $k$-scheme action, meaning $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(t,a(u,x))=a(tu,x)$ as morphism identities. If $X(k)\ne\varnothing$, then there exists $x\in X(k)$ fixed scheme-theoretically by $T$: for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $t\in T(A)$, $a_A(t,x_A)=x_A$, where $x_A$ is the scalar extension of $x$. No perfectness, infinitude, algebraic closedness, smoothness or geometric irreducibility of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, specialized to the split solvable group G_m^r. The hypothesis X(k) nonempty is essential and retained; complete means proper over k.

proof.text: Choose a $k$-group isomorphism $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ and transport the action along it. Write $H_i=\mathbf G_m^i\times\{1\}^{r-i}$ and let $C_j\simeq\mathbf G_m$ be the $j$th coordinate subgroup. Starting with a chosen $y_0\in X(k)$, construct $y_i\in X(k)$ such that the orbit morphism $H_i\to X$ of $y_i$ is the constant morphism with value $y_i$. For $i=0$ this is the unit identity. The action identity and commutativity of the product imply that the $H_i$-action commutes, as a morphism identity, with the $C_{i+1}$-action.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, multiplicative-group limit argument and induction along the split series; details made scheme-theoretic using Stacks Tags 0BX7 and 01KM.

proof.text: For the inductive step put $y=y_i$ and $f:\mathbf G_m\to X$, $f(t)=a(t,y)$, using $C_{i+1}$. Put $L=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $U=D(t)=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$. The polynomial-domain node makes $L$ integral; $U$ is dense since it contains the zero prime. The scheme $L$ is finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (one algebra generator, one affine chart), and is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian node: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$. The complement of $U$ is the single rational point $0=(t)$. Its local ring is $k[t]_{(t)}$. Every nonzero rational function is $t^n p/q$ with $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $p(0)q(0)\ne0$, by removing the lowest powers of $t$ from numerator and denominator. It lies in this local ring exactly when $n\ge0$; hence either it or its inverse lies there. Thus this stalk is a valuation ring.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, multiplicative-group limit argument and induction along the split series; details made scheme-theoretic using Stacks Tags 0BX7 and 01KM.

proof.text: Apply the valuation-point extension node with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$, source $L$, target the given proper scheme $X$, open $U$, point $0$, and morphism $f$. Step 2 verifies integral Noetherian source, density and the valuation-stalk hypothesis; properness is assumed. It gives an extension $F:V\to X$ with $U\cup\{0\}\subseteq V\subseteq L$. Since $L\setminus U=\{0\}$, $V=L$. Define $z=F(0)\in X(k)$.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, multiplicative-group limit argument and induction along the split series; details made scheme-theoretic using Stacks Tags 0BX7 and 01KM.

proof.text: On $\mathbf G_m\times L$, with coordinates $(u,t)$, compare $a(u,F(t))$ (the $C_{i+1}$-action) and $F(ut)$. Their restrictions to $D(t)=\mathbf G_m\times U$ agree by the action identity and $F|_U=f$. The source ring $k[u,u^{-1},t]$ is a domain: the polynomial-domain node gives the domain $k[u,t]$, and localization at the nonzero powers of $u$ remains a domain, since a fraction is zero only if its numerator is zero. Thus the source is reduced, and $D(t)$ is dense because it contains the zero prime. Both maps are over $k$, and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated by properness. The relative separated dense-image extension node makes the two maps equal. Pulling back along $t=0$ gives $a(u,z)=z$ as morphisms $C_{i+1}\to X$.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, multiplicative-group limit argument and induction along the split series; details made scheme-theoretic using Stacks Tags 0BX7 and 01KM.

proof.text: Compare $a(h,F(t))$ and $F(t)$ on $H_i\times L$. On $H_i\times U$, commutation and the inductive hypothesis give $a(h,F(t))=a(h,a(t,y))=a(t,a(h,y))=a(t,y)=F(t)$ as morphisms. The coordinate ring $k[h_1^{\pm1},\ldots,h_i^{\pm1},t]$ is a domain by the polynomial-domain node and the localization calculation of step 4; this also covers $i=0$. Hence the source is reduced and its open $D(t)$ is dense. Both maps are over $k$ and the target is separated by properness. Apply the relative separated dense-image extension node again, and restrict to $t=0$. The resulting morphism identity $a(h,z)=z$ says that $z$ remains fixed by $H_i$.

source.place: Theorem 16.51, printed p.343, multiplicative-group limit argument and induction along the split series; details made scheme-theoretic using Stacks Tags 0BX7 and 01KM.

proof.text: Set $y_{i+1}=z$. Multiplication identifies $H_i\times C_{i+1}$ with $H_{i+1}$, and the action identity gives $a(hc,z)=a(h,a(c,z))=a(h,z)=z$ using steps 4 and 5. This completes the induction. For $r=0$ retain $y_0$; otherwise take $x=y_r$. Its orbit morphism $T\to X$ is constant, also after transport back through the chosen isomorphism. Evaluating this morphism identity on any commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$ gives $a_A(t,x_A)=x_A$, exactly the required scheme-theoretic fixedness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q144-eaefeabe7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all six steps in full against Milne iAG Thm 16.51 (p.343: G_m limit argument and induction along the subnormal series) and every cited statement. The item is the G_m^r case, with the same hypotheses (proper = complete, X(k) nonempty kept) and scheme-theoretic fixedness on A-points, which is what the citer lem-sfb-field-maximal-split-tori-conjugacy uses. Nothing is weakened. This is a first split, not a 2026-10-21 re-split, and it creates no new nodes. Steps: (1) transport the action, set up the inductive claim that the H_i-orbit map is constant, and derive commutation from the action identity. (2) k[t] is a domain by the polynomial leaf and Noetherian by the 01T6 leaf, D(t) is dense, and the t^n p/q computation shows k[t]_(t) is a valuation ring. (3) The 0BX7 extension node (S=Spec k, Y=X proper) gives V ⊇ U ∪ {0}, so V = L and z = F(0) is in X(k). (4) and (5) apply ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated (reduced domain source, D(t) dense, X/k separated via proper) to a(u,F(t)) vs F(ut) and to a(h,F(t)) vs F(t), then restrict to t=0. (6) The multiplication isomorphism H_i×C_{i+1}≅H_{i+1} closes the induction. Edge cases checked: r=0, scaling on P^1, nonreduced X with trivial action, finite k (no density of k-points used), and translation on G_m, which shows properness is needed. Duplicates: lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point is the algebraically closed case only, and lem-sfb-split-flag-rational-fixed-scheme states something different, so neither duplicates the item. Route: the extension node is in the same unit and the rest are Mathlib leaves or definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA cited, no cycle. Batch-5: the item newly cites lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point, whose closure reaches def-trf-valuation-ring. That node is only the general valuation-ring definition (Stacks 00I9, Mathlib ValuationRing). It is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality statements or proofs, so it is genuinely outside the assumptions. Minor: steps 4-5 use affine products and the reducedness of a domain's spectrum without citing nodes; these are definitional, so I treat them as elementary. No fixes made.
